applies_why: The judge text does not weigh pressed witnesses verse by verse or invoke the stating-verse test; it merely notes that the challenged curse limb was dropped and hence no live link remains.
quote: C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase "pressed against a link" could cover only a live link or also a dropped limb; I read K-C as governing live chain-vs-chain collisions, not a dropped limb that leaves no live link.
why: The judge reasons from the limb being dropped rather than from whether any single pressed verse states the contrary, so it does not do what K-C forbids or omit what K-C requires for a live chain collision.
